summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, kidney transplant, and recurrent UTIs was admitted with fever, nausea, and foul-smelling urine. She was found to have pyelonephritis due to Klebsiella pneumoniae, mild hyperglycemia with an elevated anion gap, and acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration. She was treated with IV ceftriaxone, then transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin. Her kidney function returned to baseline, infection resolved, and metabolic parameters stabilized. She remained on her home immunosuppressants and chronic medications. She was discharged home with a full course of ciprofloxacin, instructions to hold fosfomycin until completion, and follow-up labs and transplant clinic visit.
problems: Tubulo-interstitial nephritis, not specified as acute or chronic
